findings.element: "Refine row 1: on the invoice" select — option "Memo on statement" (internally target 'private_note', api 'PrivateNote')
findings.finding: The option labeled "Memo on statement" is wired to QuickBooks Online's PrivateNote field, which is an internal-only memo that is never printed on a customer statement — the label describes a field that does not exist as named.
findings.user_impact: An accountant who picks this option expecting it to compare against the customer-facing statement memo is actually comparing against a different, internal-only field, so a refine rule set up on this assumption can silently fail to match the intended invoice or match the wrong one.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the option to match QuickBooks Online's own field name, e.g. "Memo (internal)" or "Memo (PrivateNote)", and drop "statement" since PrivateNote is never shown on a statement.

evidence.source: Accounting rule: QuickBooks Online's Invoice.PrivateNote is an internal-only memo not shown to the customer or on any statement; conflating it with a statement memo is a field-mapping error, not covered by vocabulary.md.

findings.finding: The description reads "Post the remainder as an overpayment," using "Post" where Synder's canonical term for writing data into the books is "Sync".
findings.user_impact: An accountant reading "Post" may expect a distinct journal-entry posting step separate from Synder's usual sync, creating doubt about how and when the overpayment actually lands in the books.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "...the remainder syncs as an overpayment" to stay on the canonical Sync term.

evidence.quote: Post the remainder as an overpayment.
evidence.source: vocabulary.md line 104: "Sync (Synchronization) | post, push (syncing data from Synder to books)"

findings.element: "In plain terms" read-out, "No match" line (shown when "Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice" is off)
findings.finding: When the cancel-sync switch is off, an unmatched payment is recorded as a Sales Receipt automatically, with no confirmation step and no way to tell this apart from an unapplied customer payment.
findings.user_impact: If the real invoice exists but the rule simply failed to find it (too-narrow date window, wrong reference field), the payment books as new income via a Sales Receipt while the original invoice can still be paid separately later — double-counting revenue with nothing to catch it before or after the fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit confirmation before a no-match payment is recorded as a Sales Receipt, and confirm with Product/Accounting whether an unapplied customer payment is the safer default outcome.

evidence.source: Accounting rule: booking an unmatched payment as a new Sales Receipt without confirming the matching invoice is genuinely absent from the books risks double-counting income.

gaps: Update (save/commit): the actual write-to-saved-state path is exercised in a dedicated pass, not this recon; this round's read of its validation-blocks-save behaviour comes from source inspection, not an observed interaction.

Close without saving / Discard changes: the actual discard commit path is exercised in a dedicated pass, not this recon; whether unsaved rule changes are fully discarded (vs. partially retained) was not observed interactively here.
reference_gaps: vocabulary.md has no entries for this screen's domain-specific terms ("matching", "refine row", "overpayment", "payment application"), so terminology choices specific to payment-to-invoice matching could only be checked against general accounting/QuickBooks usage, not against a canonical Synder source.
